name: Guess Who / Detective Game
concept_focus: Dictionaries, lists of dictionaries and filtering, then a machine detective that solves cases

story.title: The Lantern Street Murders
story.client: Inspector Halloran of the Lantern Street watch
story.hook: Someone on Lantern Street is wearing a stolen face. Halloran has a lineup, a stack of witness statements and no patience left. Build the game of questions that narrows the lineup, then build a detective machine that asks better questions than any of his officers.

acts.title: Act I: The Lineup
acts.goal: Suspects as data, a readable board, questions, and a crowd that shrinks with every answer.

acts.title: Act II: The Case
acts.goal: Edge cases, named functions, a final accusation and cases that can be lost.

acts.title: Act III: The Case Engine
acts.goal: Generated cases, case files, a question advisor, a machine detective and a witness who lies.

boss_lore: The False Alibi has an answer for every question. The trick is asking the one question its story cannot survive.
boss_brief: Bring a finished detective.py: generated or loaded cases with unique suspects, filtering questions with turn limits and accusations, a question advisor, a machine detective that solves cases in few questions, and a case where one witness lies.
boss_twist: The False Alibi lies once per case. Write inconsistent_witness(case) that cross-checks every witness statement against the case facts and returns the witness whose statements contradict the others, or None when everyone agrees. Your machine detective must still solve cases with one lying witness in at most six questions on average across 200 generated cases; print that average. Accusing with no suspects left, or with two still standing, must be handled without a crash.

mobs.name: The Lineup
mobs.encounter: Build the suspect roster and decide which traits each suspect needs so every one can be told apart.
mobs.contract: Eight faces under the lantern. Write each one down as data, with enough traits that no two can be mistaken for each other.

objectives.label: Build the roster
objectives.brief: In detective.py, build a list of at least eight suspects, each a dictionary with a name and the same set of traits.

objectives.label: Check they differ
objectives.brief: Write a check that no two suspects have exactly the same traits, and run it at start.

objectives.label: Explain the traits
objectives.brief: Explain how you chose traits so that a few questions can always tell suspects apart.

mobs.name: The Witness Board
mobs.concept: Looping over lists and string output
mobs.encounter: Display the remaining suspects and their traits readably and explain how the loop visits each one.
mobs.contract: Halloran's officers cannot read your notes. Pin every suspect to the board in a form anyone can scan.

objectives.label: Show the board
objectives.brief: Print every remaining suspect on one line each, with their traits lined up in columns.

objectives.label: Count the suspects
objectives.brief: Show how many suspects remain above the board.

objectives.label: Trace the loop
objectives.brief: Predict what the board prints for a list of two suspects, then check it.

mobs.name: The Interrogator
mobs.encounter: Offer a set of questions, take the player's pick and reason about which trait and value that question really checks.
mobs.contract: Every question is a lantern held up to one trait. Offer the questions, take a choice and know exactly which trait it lights.

objectives.label: Offer questions
objectives.brief: Show a numbered menu of yes-or-no questions, each linked to a trait and a value in a dictionary.

objectives.label: Take a pick
objectives.brief: Read the player's choice, reject anything not on the menu, and answer it truthfully for the hidden culprit.

objectives.label: Explain the lookup
objectives.brief: Explain how your program turns a menu number into the trait and value it checks.

mobs.name: The Vanishing Crowd
mobs.encounter: Narrow the suspects after an answer by comparing what you know before and after the question.
mobs.contract: Every answer should send someone home. Keep the suspects who still fit and let the rest vanish from the board.

objectives.label: Filter the lineup
objectives.brief: After each answer, keep only the suspects whose trait matches it, building a new list rather than removing items while looping.

objectives.label: Explain the removal trap
objectives.brief: Explain why removing items from a list while looping over it skips suspects, and show your version does not.

objectives.label: Predict who is left
objectives.brief: Predict who remains after two answers on your roster, then check it.

mobs.name: The False Lead
mobs.encounter: Handle questions that eliminate nobody or everybody and always show how many suspects remain.
mobs.contract: Some questions are traps: they clear nobody, or everybody. A good detective notices before wasting a turn.

objectives.label: Spot a useless question
objectives.brief: Warn the player when a question would not eliminate anyone, and hide questions already asked.

objectives.label: Never empty the board
objectives.brief: Explain how the lineup could become empty and make sure an honest answer can never remove the culprit.

objectives.label: Notice the last suspect
objectives.brief: When one suspect remains, say so and move straight to the accusation.

mobs.name: The Case Clerk
mobs.encounter: Split asking, answering and filtering into named behaviours and explain what each receives and hands back.
mobs.contract: The Clerk refuses to file a case written as one long ramble. Give every job its own function.

objectives.label: Write ask_question
objectives.brief: Write a function that shows the menu and returns the chosen question.

objectives.label: Write filter_suspects
objectives.brief: Write filter_suspects(suspects, trait, value, answer) that returns the new list without printing anything.

objectives.label: Explain the split
objectives.brief: Explain what each function receives and returns, and why filter_suspects should not change the list it was given.

mobs.name: The Accuser
mobs.encounter: Let the player make a final accusation and justify how the program knows whether the case is solved.
mobs.contract: Halloran does not arrest on a hunch. When you point at a face, the program must know for certain if you are right.

objectives.label: Make an accusation
objectives.brief: Let the player accuse a suspect by name at any time, matching names without caring about capitals or spaces.

objectives.label: Reveal the truth
objectives.brief: Compare the accused with the culprit, announce the result and reveal the culprit's traits.

objectives.label: Match names safely
objectives.brief: Explain what goes wrong when the player types a name that is not in the lineup, and handle it.

mobs.name: The Cold Case
mobs.concept: Turn limits, loop exits and reset state
mobs.encounter: Cap questions or wrong guesses so the case can be lost, then open a new case without leftovers from the filtered list.
mobs.contract: A case that cannot be lost is not a case. Give the player limited questions and guesses, and a clean new case after.

objectives.label: Limit the questions
objectives.brief: Allow a fixed number of questions and wrong accusations, show what is left, and lose the case when they run out.

objectives.label: Open a fresh case
objectives.brief: After a case ends, offer a new one with a new culprit and the full lineup back.

objectives.label: Catch the leftovers
objectives.brief: Explain how a new case could start with last case's filtered list, and show yours copies the full roster instead.

mobs.name: The Forger
mobs.encounter: Generate a new lineup for every case from pools of traits.
mobs.contract: Halloran is tired of the same eight faces. The Forger can make new ones by the dozen, but every one must still be unique.

objectives.label: Build trait pools
objectives.brief: Keep a dictionary of trait names to the values each can take, and a pool of names.

objectives.label: Forge a lineup
objectives.brief: Generate a lineup of a chosen size with random traits, retrying any suspect who would duplicate another.

objectives.label: Refuse an impossible size
objectives.brief: Explain why asking for more suspects than there are trait combinations would loop forever, and stop it.

mobs.name: The Clue Weaver
mobs.encounter: Store hand-written cases in a file and load them.
mobs.contract: The watch keeps its best cases in a ledger. Read cases from a file, so new ones can be written without touching the code.

objectives.label: Write a case file
objectives.brief: Save a case (its suspects, questions and culprit) to a JSON file.

objectives.label: Load a case
objectives.brief: Let the player choose between a generated case and one loaded from the file.

objectives.label: Reject a bad case
objectives.brief: Check a loaded case is valid (the culprit is in the lineup, every suspect has every trait) and explain each check.

mobs.name: The Splitter
mobs.concept: Scoring questions by how well they split
mobs.encounter: Recommend the question that cuts the lineup most evenly.
mobs.contract: The best question is not the clever one. It is the one that sends half the suspects home whatever the answer.

objectives.label: Count both answers
objectives.brief: For every unasked question, count how many suspects a yes and a no would leave.

objectives.label: Recommend the best
objectives.brief: Add a hint command that recommends the question whose worst case leaves the fewest suspects.

objectives.label: Explain halving
objectives.brief: Explain why a question that splits the lineup in half finds the culprit in about log2(n) questions.

mobs.name: The Machine Detective
mobs.concept: An agent that plays the game itself
mobs.encounter: Let a bot solve cases on its own and measure how well it does.
mobs.contract: Halloran wants a detective that never sleeps. Your advisor already knows the best question; let it ask, listen and accuse on its own.

objectives.label: Let the bot play
objectives.brief: Write a function that plays a whole case with no input(): it asks the best question, filters, and accuses when one suspect remains.

objectives.label: Solve 200 cases
objectives.brief: Run it on 200 generated cases and report the average and worst number of questions.

objectives.label: Compare with yourself
objectives.brief: Compare its average with your own games and explain where your questions were worse.

mobs.name: The Liar's Clause
mobs.encounter: One witness may lie once; still find the culprit.
mobs.contract: One witness on Lantern Street lies, once, about one thing. Filtering hard on every answer now sends the culprit home. Keep anyone who fits all but one answer.

objectives.label: Add a liar
objectives.brief: Add a mode where exactly one answer during the case is a lie, chosen at random.

objectives.label: Allow one contradiction
objectives.brief: Track, for each suspect, how many answers they contradict, and keep everyone with at most one.

objectives.label: Explain the cost
objectives.brief: Explain why one possible lie means you need extra questions, and how your machine detective copes with it.

mobs.name: The Archive
mobs.concept: Session records and a front desk
mobs.encounter: Keep solved-case statistics and give the game a menu.
mobs.contract: Every solved case goes in the archive, with how many questions it took. Give Halloran a front desk to start any kind of case.

objectives.label: Archive the results
objectives.brief: Save each finished case's result and question count to a JSON archive and show the player's record.

objectives.label: Open the front desk
objectives.brief: Add a menu: play a generated case, play a filed case, watch the machine detective, liar mode, or quit.

objectives.label: Predict the record
objectives.brief: Predict the solve rate and average questions after three cases you play, then check the archive shows the same.
